What your BWSSB water bill should look like

BAF analysed actual BWSSB bills from apartment communities across Bengaluru. Here is what we found — so you can verify your own bill.

🙏 A warm thank you to the Executive Council members of BAF who shared their apartment's BWSSB bills for this research. Your willingness to share real data has made it possible to confirm these findings and help hundreds of apartment communities across Bengaluru understand and verify their own bills.
50%
Sanitary Charges = 50% of Cauvery water charge Confirmed across every single bill analysed — 5 complexes, 9 bills. S.C. for Borewell is a separate fixed charge (₹625/HP or ₹130/flat) on top. If your Sanitary ÷ Water ≠ 0.50, question it with your BWSSB Sub Division.

Key Findings

What the data shows

Six clear patterns emerged from analysing bills across different complex sizes, locations and billing periods.

50%
"ಒಳಚರಂಡಿ ವೆಚ್ಚ / Sanitary Charges" on your bill
This line on your BWSSB bill is the monthly sewage charge — what you pay for BWSSB to carry away and treat the wastewater from your complex through their Underground Drainage (UGD) network.

Why is it levied? When water enters your complex, it eventually leaves as sewage. BWSSB maintains the underground pipes, pumping stations and sewage treatment plants that handle this. The sanitary charge is how they recover that cost from you.

Why 50%? BWSSB charges 50% of your Cauvery water charge as sanitary — because that water returns as sewage to their underground drainage (UGD) network, and BWSSB carries and treats it. This rate started at 25% in Apr 2025 and ramped up by 6.25% every quarter, reaching 50% by May 2026. Our analysis of 9 bills across 5 complexes confirms this ratio is applied exactly — to the rupee — every single time.

When it should be ₹0: If your complex has an STP (Sewage Treatment Plant) that treats wastewater and discharges it outside the BWSSB UGD network (to a lake, park or reuse system), BWSSB should not levy this charge — you are not using their sewage infrastructure. If you are being charged, write to your BWSSB AEE/EE with STP records.
₹0
STP complexes can be exempt from sanitary charges
Complexes with an STP that does NOT discharge into BWSSB's UGD network should pay ₹0 sanitary. If you're being charged, write to your BWSSB AEE/EE.
10%
What puts you in Partial ND category?
If your complex has a swimming pool, gymnasium, clubhouse, party hall or any commercial shop, BWSSB classifies you as Partial Non-Domestic (HR). BWSSB then treats a minimum percentage of your total water consumption as commercial use — billed at higher non-domestic rates — even if the pool and gym actually use far less.

The minimum ND% has changed:
• Apr 2025 tariff order: minimum ND% = 25%
• Sep 2025 tariff order: revised down to 10% (following BAF's representation at the 01.07.2025 meeting)

How the ND% affects your water charge: BWSSB splits your total consumption into two portions — ND% at higher non-domestic slab rates, and the rest at domestic HR rates. The higher the ND%, the more of your consumption is billed at the expensive non-domestic rate. Example: at 10% ND, 100 KL of a 1,000 KL bill goes at ND rates. At 25% ND, 250 KL goes at ND rates — a substantially higher bill for the same consumption.

Complexes that haven't been re-assessed since Apr 2025 may still be billed at 25% ND — check your bill's ND split and request correction if needed. Your ND% should be visible on your BWSSB connection documents or Demand Note.
2
Two billing schemes in use simultaneously
Two tariff orders are in effect simultaneously:

Apr 2025 scheme (volume slabs only): Water charge based on actual KL consumed — slabs at ₹25/₹28/₹32/₹55 per KL. Applied to complexes with fewer than 200 flats.

Sep 2025 scheme (flat-norm minimum): For 200+ flat complexes, a minimum consumption is set by flat count (e.g. 300 flats → minimum 1.8 ML/month at ₹32/KL). Consumption beyond the minimum is billed at ₹55/KL. If actual consumption is below the minimum, the minimum charge still applies.

BWSSB decides which scheme applies — you cannot choose. The Sep 2025 scheme was introduced after BAF's representation on 01.07.2025 for fairer billing based on flat count, not just raw consumption.
₹625
Borewell: ₹625/HP or ₹130/flat
BWSSB uses one of two methods — whichever was set at the time of your connection registration. Check your original connection documents to know which applies.
₹1,500
Meter charge is fixed
Fixed monthly fee determined by your connection's pipe bore size — set at registration, never changes. Per Clause 28, BWSSB Water Supply Regulations:

₹300/month → 32mm pipe  |  ₹750/month → 40mm pipe
₹1,000/month → 50mm pipe  |  ₹1,500/month → 100mm pipe

Larger complexes with higher demand get larger bore pipes at connection, hence higher meter charges. Not related to consumption.
HR vs ND
Domestic HR and Partial ND have completely different sanitary formulas
Domestic HR (no pool/gym/clubhouse):
Sanitary = ₹130 per flat per month × number of flats — fixed, does not change with consumption, month, or how much water you use.
✓ Confirmed: Complex F (120 flats) — sanitary = ₹15,600 = 120 × ₹130, identical in both months.

Partial ND (has pool/gym/clubhouse):
The bill has two separate sewerage-related lines — with completely different logic:

• Sanitary Charges (50% of Cauvery water charge) — BWSSB gives you Cauvery water; you return sewage to their UGD. BWSSB charges 50% of your water charge for carrying and treating that sewage. (Ramped up from 25% in Apr 2025 — reached 50% by May 2026.)
• S.C. for Borewell — BWSSB assumes borewell water also ends up as sewage in their UGD. They levy a fixed monthly charge on your registered borewell, shown as a separate line: ₹625/HP/month OR ₹130/flat/month — whichever basis was set at the time of your BWSSB registration.

These two lines are billed separately for a reason — the logic and dispute path for each is entirely different.

✓ Confirmed: 9 bills across 5 complexes.

💡 Key point: If your borewell is not operational, you can challenge the S.C. for Borewell charge. Provide evidence to your Sub Division AEE that the borewell is defunct — BWSSB should remove the ₹625/HP (or ₹130/flat) levy.

⚠ Exception: When flat count is large and Cauvery consumption is low, the ₹130/flat floor can dominate over the 25%-of-water calculation — making sanitary appear near-fixed. See the Complex H Case Study tab for a full decode.
Disclaimer: This analysis is based on actual BWSSB bills shared voluntarily with BAF for research purposes. All analysis is indicative — BWSSB's billing is the definitive reference. Rates cited are per official BWSSB orders and Karnataka Government notifications. BAF does not set, determine, or guarantee any of these charges. Always verify with your actual BWSSB bill and Demand Note. · BWSSB Helpline: 1916 · Portal: owc.bwssb.gov.in

Bill Guide

How to read your BWSSB water bill

Every line on your BWSSB bill explained in plain language — what it means, how it is calculated, and what to check.

🪪 Top Section — Who you are
Sub Division Name / ಉಪ ವಿಭಾಗ
The BWSSB office that manages your area. This is who you contact for complaints, meter issues, and billing disputes.
💡 Note this down — you'll need it when writing to your AEE/EE.
RR No. / ಆರ್.ಆರ್.ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ
Your Revenue Register Number — the unique ID for your water connection. Like a bank account number for your water supply. Quote this in every communication with BWSSB.
💡 Keep this number handy. Required for online payments and complaints.
Consumer ID and Type / ಬಲಕೆದಾರರ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಮತ್ತು ನಮೂನೆ
Your consumer number and billing category. For apartments with a pool/gym/clubhouse this will read "Partial ND Apartments". For apartments without these, it will read "Domestic HR Apartments". Your category determines which tariff rates apply.
⚠ If your category seems wrong, contact your Sub Division — wrong category = wrong rates.
Meter Reading Date / ಮೀಟರ್ ಓದಿದ ದಿನಾಂಕ
The date BWSSB read your meter for this bill. Your bill covers the period from the previous reading date to this date.
💧 Consumption Details — How much water you used
Present Reading / ಇಂದಿನ ವಾಚನ
The meter reading this month — in litres (the big number on the meter dial).
Previous Reading / ಹಿಂದಿನ ವಾಚನ
The meter reading last month.
Consumption Lts / ಬಳಸಿದ ನೀರಿನ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ
Present Reading minus Previous Reading = litres consumed this month. Divide by 1,000 to get Kilolitres (KL). Divide by your number of flats and by 30 to get average litres per flat per day.
Consumption Lts ÷ 1,000 = KL  |  KL ÷ Flats ÷ 30 = L/flat/day
⚠ If L/flat/day is below 50 or above 600, something is likely wrong with the meter reading. Raise a dispute.
💰 Payment Details — What you owe and why
Water Charges / ನೀರಿನ ವೆಚ್ಚ
The core charge for the water you consumed. This is the largest line on your bill and the base for your sanitary charge. How it is calculated depends on your category:

Domestic HR (no pool/gym/clubhouse): Your total consumption is billed at domestic HR slab rates (₹25/₹28/₹32/₹55 per KL). Straightforward — one rate structure, one calculation.

Partial ND HR (has pool/gym/clubhouse): BWSSB splits your total consumption into two portions and bills each at a different rate:
• ND portion (minimum 10% of total consumption, per Sep 2025 order) — billed at the higher Non-Domestic slab rates (₹60/₹70/₹80/₹95/₹98/₹99 per KL)
• Domestic HR portion (the remaining 90%) — billed at domestic HR slab rates (₹25/₹28/₹32/₹55 per KL)

The ND% applied to your complex is set at registration. The minimum is 10% (Sep 2025 order) but your complex may have been registered at a higher ND% — check your BWSSB connection documents. The higher the ND%, the higher your water charge for the same consumption.

Example: 1,000 KL total, 10% ND split → 100 KL billed at ND rates + 900 KL at domestic HR rates. If your ND% were 25% → 250 KL at ND rates + 750 KL at domestic HR rates — a significantly higher bill for the same consumption.
Partial ND Water = (ND% × consumption × ND slab rate) + ((100−ND%) × consumption × Domestic HR slab rate)
💡 Your ND% is fixed at registration — ask your Sub Division AEE what ND% is on your connection. If it is above 10%, you may be able to request a revision to the new minimum.
Meter Charges / ಮಾಪಕ ವೆಚ್ಚ
A fixed monthly fee for maintaining the water meter. Determined entirely by the pipe bore size set at the time of your BWSSB connection — never changes month to month. Common values seen on apartment bills:

₹300/month → 32mm (1.25") pipe
₹750/month → 40mm (1.5") pipe
₹1,000/month → 50mm (2") pipe
₹1,500/month → 100mm (4") pipe

Larger apartments with higher water demand get a larger bore at registration, hence a higher meter charge. Your bore size is fixed at connection — check your original BWSSB connection documents.
💡 If your meter charge has changed, query your Sub Division — it should never change unless the physical meter was replaced with a different bore size.
Sanitary Charges / ಒಳಚರಂಡಿ ವೆಚ್ಚ
The charge BWSSB levies for carrying and treating your complex's sewage through their underground drainage (UGD) network. Your bill has two separate sewerage-related charges — each with its own logic:

① Sanitary Charges — charged because BWSSB supplies you Cauvery water, which eventually returns as sewage to their UGD. BWSSB charges 50% of your Cauvery water charge for this service (ramped from 25% in Apr 2025, reaching 50% by May 2026). For Domestic HR, a minimum of ₹130/flat applies — whichever is higher.

② S.C. for Borewell — if your complex has a borewell, BWSSB assumes that water also drains into their UGD as sewage. They levy a fixed monthly charge on your borewell, shown as a separate line on the bill: ₹625/HP/month OR ₹130/flat/month — whichever basis was registered with BWSSB at the time of your connection.

These two charges are entirely separate — different justifications, different dispute paths.

Domestic HR (no pool/gym): Sanitary = MAX(25% of water, ₹130 × flats). Fixed if the ₹130/flat floor dominates.
Partial ND (has pool/gym): Sanitary = 50% of Cauvery water charge.

If your complex has an STP that does NOT drain into BWSSB's UGD, Sanitary Charges should be ₹0 — write to your AEE/EE if charged incorrectly.
If your borewell is not operational, challenge the S.C. for Borewell charge with evidence to your Sub Division AEE — BWSSB should remove the ₹625/HP or ₹130/flat levy entirely.
Sanitary Charges = 50% of Cauvery water (min ₹130/flat for HR)  +  Borewell SC = ₹625/HP or ₹130/flat (separate fixed charge — disputable if borewell defunct)
✓ These are two separate lines on your bill. Check each independently. A defunct borewell = grounds to remove the S.C. for Borewell charge entirely.
S.C. for Borewell / ಕೊಳವೆ ಬಾವಿ ಶ್ಯಾನಿಟರಿ ವೆಚ್ಚ
The monthly charge for using borewell water in addition to BWSSB supply. BWSSB calculates this in one of two ways — whichever was set when your connection was registered:

Method 1 — Per flat: Number of flats × ₹130/month
Method 2 — Per HP: Total borewell motor HP × ₹625/month

The borewell charge stays the same every month regardless of how much borewell water you use.
Borewell SC ÷ Flats = ₹130 (Method 1)  OR  Borewell SC ÷ ₹625 = HP (Method 2)
💡 If you have no borewell, this should be ₹0.
Other Charges / ಇತರ ವೆಚ್ಚ
A catch-all field for penalties and special levies. Should be ₹0 on a normal bill. If non-zero, the reason is not printed in the billing table — BWSSB prints it as a remark below the barcode at the bottom of the bill slip. Always check the footer.

Known penalty types seen on BAF member bills:
• LEVY OF CHARGES TOWARDS RWH — Rainwater Harvesting system not installed. Mandatory for all buildings above 1,200 sq ft (BWSSB Act 2009, Section 72-A). Per BWSSB (RWH Amendment) Regulations 2015: penalty is 25% of total water + sanitary charges for first 3 months, then escalates to 50% until RWH is installed.
• LEVY OF CHARGES TOWARDS OC — Occupancy Certificate not obtained. Levied under BWSSB circular dated March 3, 2016, reinforced by Supreme Court directive to deny utilities to buildings without OC. Observed on bills as a near-fixed monthly levy that can be 3–5× the water charge — does not scale proportionally with consumption. Exact rate formula not published; BAF is pursuing this with BWSSB.
⚠ If Other Charges is non-zero, read the footer below the barcode on your bill slip to find out why. Raise the issue with your Sub Division AEE immediately.
Arrears / ಹಿಂದಿನ ಬಾಕಿ
Any unpaid amount from previous months. Should be ₹0 if you paid your last bill in full. If this is non-zero, check your payment receipts.
Interest on Arrears / ಬಡ್ಡಿ
Penalty interest on unpaid arrears. Should be ₹0 if your account is current. Pay on time to avoid this.
Total Amount / ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೊತ್ತ
The sum of all charges above. This is what you pay by the due date. After the due date, an additional late payment charge applies (shown at the bottom of the bill as "Amount Payable After Due Date").
Water + Meter + Sanitary + Borewell SC + Others + Arrears + Interest = Total
📋 Previous Month Payment — Proof your last bill was paid
Receipt No. / Pay Date / Amount / Mode / Paid at
Confirms that your previous month's bill was received and recorded by BWSSB. If the amount shown here does not match what you actually paid, contact your Sub Division with your payment receipt.
💡 Always keep payment receipts for at least 12 months.

Billing Logic

Sanitary Charges — All Scenarios

The sanitary charge on your bill depends on three factors: whether you have Cauvery water, a borewell, and an STP — and crucially, where the treated water goes. BWSSB charges only for sewage that enters their UGD network. If nothing enters the UGD, the charge is zero. Here are all the permutations.

💡 The core logic: BWSSB charges 50% of your Cauvery water charge as sanitary — because that water returns as sewage to their UGD and they carry and treat it. Separately, if you have a borewell, they add a fixed levy of ₹625/HP/month or ₹130/flat/month (whichever was set at registration) on the same logic — borewell water is also assumed to drain to their UGD. The only way to reduce or eliminate sanitary charges is to prove that sewage is NOT entering their UGD — either because you have an STP that fully treats and reuses it within your premises, or because your borewell is defunct.
# Your Setup Sanitary Charges
(25% of Cauvery water)		 S.C. for Borewell
(₹625/HP or ₹130/flat — as registered)		 Key condition & action
A Cauvery only
No borewell · No STP		 25% of water charge
(min ₹130/flat for HR)		 ₹0 All Cauvery sewage goes to UGD. Standard billing. Nothing to dispute.
B Cauvery + STP
No borewell · STP drains to UGD		 25% of water charge ₹0 STP treats the sewage but treated water still enters BWSSB's UGD. BWSSB carries it — sanitary applies in full.
C Cauvery + STP
No borewell · Treated water 100% reused within premises		 ₹0 Exempt ₹0 Nothing enters UGD — BWSSB has nothing to carry or treat. Both charges = ₹0. Must prove to AEE with STP certification and drainage layout showing zero UGD discharge.
D Cauvery + Borewell
No STP		 25% of water charge ₹625/HP or ₹130/flat Both Cauvery and borewell sewage go to UGD. Both charges apply. Rate depends on what was registered with BWSSB. Complex H = ₹625/HP
E Cauvery + Borewell + STP
STP drains to UGD		 25% of water charge ₹625/HP or ₹130/flat STP treats sewage but treated water goes to UGD. BWSSB still carries it. Both charges apply in full.
F Cauvery + Borewell + STP
Treated water 100% reused within premises		 ₹0 Exempt ₹0 Exempt STP treats ALL sewage (Cauvery + borewell). 100% reused for garden, flushing etc. Nothing to UGD. Both charges = ₹0. Must prove to AEE — STP certification, drainage layout, borewell connection diagram.
G Cauvery + Borewell + STP
STP treats borewell only · Cauvery sewage to UGD		 25% of water charge ₹0 Exempt Cauvery sewage still enters UGD — sanitary applies. Borewell is fully treated and reused within premises — borewell SC = ₹0. Must prove borewell water is fully reused.
H Cauvery + Borewell
Borewell defunct / not operational		 25% of water charge ₹0 Exempt If borewell is no longer in use, challenge the borewell SC (₹625/HP or ₹130/flat — whichever applies) with evidence: motor removed, borewell sealed, no-use certificate. Write to Sub Division AEE to get borewell deregistered from your connection.
⚠️ Important: The exemptions in scenarios C, F, and G require you to actively prove your case to BWSSB — they will not apply automatically. You need written certification from a BWSSB-empanelled agency confirming your STP is functional and that treated water is fully reused within your premises with zero UGD discharge. Without this documentation, BWSSB will continue billing the standard charges.

Action Checklist

Check your own bill

Use this checklist to verify your BWSSB Partial ND bill. Tap each item to mark it done.

📋 Your BWSSB Bill Verification Checklist
✓
Verify sanitary = 50% of water charge
Divide the Sanitary Charges line by your Water Charges. The answer should be 0.50 (50%). The Borewell SC is a separate fixed charge — check it independently: divide by ₹625 to get HP, or divide by number of flats to check if it equals ₹130.
Partial ND: Sanitary ÷ Water = 0.50 (50%)  |  Borewell SC ÷ HP = ₹625 or ÷ Flats = ₹130  |  Domestic HR: Sanitary ÷ Flats = ₹130
✓
Check your borewell charge basis
Divide borewell SC by number of flats. If it equals ₹130, you're on per-flat basis. If not, divide by ₹625 — the result is the HP being charged.
Borewell SC ÷ Flats = ₹130 (or) Borewell SC ÷ ₹625 = HP
✓
If you have an STP — check if sanitary is ₹0
If your STP treats sewage and it does NOT drain into BWSSB's Underground Drainage (UGD) network, sanitary charges should be ₹0. If BWSSB is charging you, write to your AEE/EE.
STP (not to UGD) → Sanitary = ₹0
✓
Verify meter reading is realistic
Divide consumption (litres) by number of flats and by 30. This gives average litres per flat per day. Should be 100–400 L/flat/day for a typical apartment.
Consumption Lts ÷ Flats ÷ 30 = L/flat/day (expect 100–400)
✓
Use the BAF Calculator for a full estimate
Compare your actual bill with the BAF Cauvery Cost & Monthly Bill Calculator to spot any discrepancies.
tinyurl.com/BWSSB-Calc
✓
If anything doesn't match — write to your BWSSB AEE/EE
Contact the Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) or Executive Engineer (EE) of your BWSSB Sub Division. Include your RR Number, the bill in question, and your specific query.
BWSSB Helpline: 1916 · Portal: owc.bwssb.gov.in
ℹ BAF Tip: Keep 3–6 months of BWSSB bills together. Patterns like a sudden spike in consumption (possible meter issue) or a change in sanitary ratio are easier to spot across multiple months.

Government Orders & Regulations

All BWSSB tariff orders, regulations and circulars that govern water billing for Bengaluru apartments. Download for your records or share with your AEE when disputing a bill.

📋
Bulk Water Tariff Revision — Apartments & PG
BWSSB Notification No. BWSSB/C/EIC/CE(S)/DCE(M)-1/542 /2025-26  ·  Dated 01.09.2025  ·  PDF available
The primary tariff order governing apartment water billing from September 2025. Introduced flat-norm minimum billing for large complexes and revised the minimum ND% downward for Partial ND. BAF represented at the 01.07.2025 board meeting that led to this revision.
  • Domestic HR <200 flats: volume slabs at ₹25 / ₹28 / ₹32 / ₹55 per KL
  • Domestic HR 200+ flats: flat-norm minimum (e.g. 300 flats → 1.8 ML/month at ₹32/KL; excess at ₹55/KL)
  • Minimum ND% for Partial ND reduced from 25% → 10%
  • Hostels and PG charges revised (Column E rates)
  • Effective: water W.E.F. 01.08.2025 · billing W.E.F. 01.09.2025
⬇ Download PDF
📊
Revised Water Tariff — Ready Reckoner 2025
BWSSB  ·  W.E.F. 01.04.2025 (consumption) · Billing W.E.F. 01.05.2025  ·  PDF available
The first major tariff revision since 2014. Covers all consumer categories with full slab tables, sanitary charge formulas, borewell charges, meter service charges by pipe size, and a worked Partial ND-HR example. The Apr 2025 slabs still apply to complexes not yet migrated to the Sep 2025 flat-norm scheme.
  • Domestic HR slabs: 0–200 KL ₹25 · 200–500 ₹28 · 500–1000 ₹32 · 1000+ parity with domestic
  • Sanitary for Domestic HR: MAX(25%→31.25% of water, ₹130/flat) — quarterly ramp, floor ₹130/flat
  • Borewell SC: ₹130/flat OR ₹625/HP — whichever basis was set at registration (Clause 2, Sewerage Regs 1974). Check your BWSSB connection documents to confirm which applies.
  • Meter charges by pipe bore: ₹300 (32mm) · ₹1,000 (50mm) · ₹1,500 (100mm) per Clause 28
  • Minimum ND% for Partial ND set at 25% (revised to 10% in Sep 2025 order)
  • Penalties for RWH / OC / STP non-compliance: "existing rates remain the same"
  • 3% automatic annual tariff increase every 1st April

🌧️
RWH Amendment Regulations 2015 — Penalty for No Rainwater Harvesting
Notification No. BWSSB/C/CAO-S/4136/2015-16  ·  Dated 25.02.2016  ·  External link
The regulation that defines the "LEVY OF CHARGES TOWARDS RWH" penalty appearing on bills as Other Charges. Substitutes Regulation 8 of the BWSSB (Rain Water Harvesting) Regulations 2010. A 2019 amendment further doubled the rates — the 2025 tariff orders confirm existing rates apply unchanged.
  • Residential buildings: 25% of total water + sanitary charges for first 3 months → 50% thereafter until RWH is installed
  • Non-residential buildings: 50% for first 3 months → 100% thereafter
  • RWH mandatory under BWSSB Act 2009 Section 72-A: all buildings ≥ 1,200 sq ft (new) or ≥ 2,400 sq ft (pre-2009)
  • No penalty without prior opportunity of being heard (due process clause)
  • 2019 amendment doubled rates: residential 25%→50% / 50%→100%; non-residential 50%→100% / 100%→200%
  • Includes full RWH guidelines: rooftop harvesting, recharge structures, storage tank sizing
↗ Open PDF (External) Hosted by urbanwaters.in — BWSSB official compilation
🏛️
OC Penalty Circular — Penalty for No Occupancy Certificate
BWSSB Internal Circular  ·  Dated 03.03.2016  ·  RTI required
The circular that authorises the "LEVY OF CHARGES TOWARDS OC" penalty appearing on bills as Other Charges. The circular itself is not publicly available online — BWSSB's website disallows automated access and the document has not been indexed elsewhere. What is known is from news reports and affected members' bills.
⚠️ Document not publicly available. BAF recommends filing an RTI with BWSSB to obtain the full text of this circular, including the exact penalty rate formula and the basis for computation. Members currently paying OC penalties should request a written explanation from their Sub Division AEE citing the specific circular and rate applied to their bill.
  • Basis: BWSSB circular dated 03.03.2016, reinforced by Supreme Court directive to deny utilities to buildings without OC
  • Penalty appears as "Other Charges" in billing table — reason only visible in footer below barcode: "LEVY OF CHARGES TOWARDS OC"
  • Reported rate: 50% of water charges for residential · 100% for commercial (ground+2 floors and above)
  • Exemption: buildings with only ground + first floor
  • From bills analysed: penalty appears near-fixed regardless of consumption — does not scale proportionally with water charge
  • Exact formula and computation base: unconfirmed from official source — RTI pending
📬 File RTI with BWSSB Chief Engineer (Maintenance) · Cauvery Bhavan, K.G. Road, Bengaluru 560 009
💡 BAF Tip: Always keep a copy of the relevant tariff order when disputing a bill with your BWSSB Sub Division. Quoting the notification number and clause gives your representation formal standing. For OC penalty disputes specifically, request the AEE to show the circular and confirm the rate formula in writing.

Case Study

Complex H — An Exception Decoded

Complex H is a Partial ND HR apartment with a borewell, a pending OC, and unusually low Cauvery consumption relative to its flat count. These four factors interact in ways that make the bill look confusing. This tab decodes it line by line.

Complex profile: 113 flats · South Bengaluru · 18-year-old complex (occupied March 2008) · Partial ND HR billing · 28.5 HP borewell · Sub Division S13
OC situation: Builder collected ~₹90L from flat owners as BWSSB deposit but never paid BWSSB. Complex filed a High Court case against the builder. BWSSB connection obtained in 2024 after members collected again (~₹90L+). OC penalty levied from day one of connection — compounding monthly.

Bill Comparison — Jan, Mar & Jun 2026

Line Item Jan 2026 Mar 2026 Jun 2026 Notes
Consumption (KL) 193 118 194 Cauvery metered consumption only. Borewell not metered.
Water Charges ₹7,115 ₹4,250 ₹7,411 Billed on Partial ND slabs — 90% domestic-HR rate, 10% ND rate. Varies with consumption.
Meter Charges ₹1,000 ₹1,000 ₹1,000 Fixed. 50mm pipe bore (Clause 28). Never changes.
Sanitary Charges ₹16,217 ₹15,715 ₹16,529 See decode below ↓
Borewell SC ₹17,815 ₹17,815 ₹17,815 Fixed. 28.5 HP × ₹625/HP = ₹17,813 ≈ ₹17,815. Never changes.
Other Charges (OC Penalty) ₹24,645 ₹21,990 ₹25,298 See decode below ↓
Arrears / Interest ₹0 ₹0 ₹0 Paid on time each month. ✓
Total Amount ₹66,792 ₹60,770 ₹67,953 ₹591 / ₹538 / ₹601 per flat
Without OC penalty ₹42,147 ₹38,780 ₹42,655 What the bill would be if OC were in order: ₹373 / ₹343 / ₹377 per flat

🔍 Why does Sanitary look near-fixed despite varying consumption?

The bill has two separate sewerage charges:
• Sanitary Charges — 50% of Cauvery water charge (the rate ramped from 25% in Apr 2025 to 50% by May 2026). This is where the near-fixed pattern appears.
• S.C. for Borewell — a fixed monthly charge: ₹17,815 = 28.5 HP × ₹625/HP. Completely independent of consumption — never changes.

For the Cauvery sanitary, BWSSB also has a minimum of ₹130/flat/month. Whichever is higher — 25% of water charge or the per-flat minimum — gets charged. Complex H has 113 flats, so the minimum is 113 × ₹130 = ₹14,690/month.

Complex H's Cauvery water charge ranges only ₹4,250–₹7,411. Even 25% of the highest month is ₹1,853 — far below ₹14,690. So the per-flat minimum wins every single month, and sanitary stays near ₹15,000–₹16,500 regardless of consumption.

✅ This is not a billing error, and not a contradiction of the 50% rule. Both the 50% rate and the ₹130/flat minimum exist in the tariff — whichever gives a higher number applies. For Complex H, the minimum wins. If the complex significantly increases its Cauvery consumption in future, the water-based 50% will eventually overtake the minimum and sanitary will start varying again.

📌 Note on STP & sanitary: The Karnataka Government's March 2024 GO exempts apartments with fewer than 120 flats from installing an STP. Complex H (113 flats) qualifies for this exemption. But this is precisely why they pay full sanitary — without an STP, all their sewage flows directly into BWSSB's underground drainage (UGD) network, and BWSSB charges for carrying and treating it. The STP exemption and the sanitary charge are two sides of the same coin: smaller complexes don't treat their own sewage, so BWSSB does it for them and bills accordingly.

🔍 What is the OC penalty and how is it calculated?

The "Other Charges" field on the bill carries no label. The reason appears only in the footer below the barcode: "LEVY OF CHARGES TOWARDS OC". This is a penalty for not submitting an Occupancy Certificate to BWSSB, levied under a BWSSB circular dated 03.03.2016 and reinforced by Supreme Court directive.

Month Water Standard Charges
Water+Meter+Sanitary+Borewell		 Standard/flat OC Penalty OC/flat OC as % of water OC as % of standard Total/flat
Jan 2026 ₹7,115 ₹42,147 ₹373 ₹24,645 ₹218 346% 58.5% ₹591
Mar 2026 ₹4,250 ₹38,780 ₹343 ₹21,990 ₹195 517% 56.7% ₹538
Jun 2026 ₹7,411 ₹42,755 ₹378 ₹25,298 ₹224 341% 59.2% ₹601

Standard charges breakdown (what Complex H would pay without OC penalty):

ComponentJan 2026% of standardMar 2026% of standardJun 2026% of standardNature
Water Charges₹7,11516.9%₹4,25011.0%₹7,41117.3%Varies with consumption
Meter Charges₹1,0002.4%₹1,0002.6%₹1,0002.3%Fixed — 50mm pipe
Sanitary Charges₹16,21738.5%₹15,71540.5%₹16,52938.7%Near-fixed — ₹130/flat floor
Borewell SC₹17,81542.3%₹17,81545.9%₹17,81541.7%Fixed — 28.5 HP × ₹625
Standard Total₹42,147100%₹38,780100%₹42,755100%₹373 / ₹343 / ₹378 per flat
OC Penalty₹24,64558.5%₹21,99056.7%₹25,29859.2%₹218 / ₹195 / ₹224 per flat

Key observations from the data:

  • OC penalty as % of water charge alone: wildly inconsistent (341%–517%) — definitely not computed on water charge
  • Consumption dropped 38% from Jan to Mar but penalty dropped only 11% — definitely not consumption-based
  • OC penalty as % of standard charges (water + meter + sanitary + borewell): 56.7%–59.2% — variance of only 2.5 percentage points across 3 months — the most consistent pattern found
  • Within the standard bill, borewell SC dominates at 42–46% — because Cauvery consumption is so low, water is only 11–17% of the standard bill
  • Without OC penalty, this complex would pay ₹343–₹378/flat/month — a reasonable amount. The OC penalty adds ₹195–₹224/flat on top
🔍 Best hypothesis on OC penalty formula: Based on reverse engineering across 3 months, the OC penalty appears to be computed as approximately 58% of total standard charges (water + meter + sanitary + borewell SC combined). This is the only base that produces a consistent ratio. However, this has not been confirmed from any official source — the BWSSB circular dated 03.03.2016 is not publicly available.

⚠️ BAF recommends filing an RTI to obtain the circular and confirm the exact formula. Until then, this 58%-of-standard-charges hypothesis is the closest approximation from actual bill data.

✅ What Complex H should do

  1. Continue paying bills on time — arrears and interest will compound the problem further. All 3 months show ₹0 arrears — this is correct.
  2. Pursue the High Court case — the builder's failure to remit the collected BWSSB deposit is the root cause. A favourable order may allow OC regularisation.
  3. Write to BWSSB AEE (Sub Division S13) — request written confirmation of: (a) the circular under which OC penalty is levied, (b) the exact formula and computation base, (c) whether a waiver or reduction is possible given the builder fraud and ongoing litigation.
  4. File RTI with BWSSB — request the full text of BWSSB circular dated 03.03.2016 on OC penalty. Address: Chief Engineer (Maintenance), BWSSB, Cauvery Bhavan, K.G. Road, Bengaluru 560 009.
  5. Raise with BAF — BAF can take this up with the BWSSB Chairman as a systemic issue affecting apartments where builders collected but did not remit the BWSSB deposit. Complex H's case is a strong data point for this representation.
  6. Do not dispute the sanitary charge — the sanitary amount is correct per the tariff order (₹130/flat floor + ND portion). Disputing it will not succeed and may delay resolution of the OC issue.
